item: incident: truncated /work/aupai/eval/readout_30b.py to 0 bytes on the pod
basis: Pushed a patched readout with `~/bin/pod "... cat > /tmp/b0/readout.py" < eval/readout_30b.py`. The redirect resolved against the pod's cwd (/work/aupai) rather than the /tmp path I intended, so it opened eval/readout_30b.py for writing and truncated it; the heredoc content never arrived, leaving 0 bytes. item: defect: BUDGET_MISMATCH_LIMIT refuses the 16B-vs-8B progress pair it should permit
verdict: confirmed by running it; found while re-running the 16B readout
basis: readout_30b.py:405-417 refuses when the two token budgets differ by more than 5%. On the 7.5 PROGRESS track the budget gap IS the treatment -- 16.056B vs 7.799B is 51.4%, so the gate refuses every progress read by construction. It is correct on the retention/OOD track, where a budget gap is a confound. The gate tests 'do the budgets differ' as a proxy for 'is the difference confounded', and which one it is depends on the track, which the gate cannot see. Both the harness milestone path and my re-run omitted --actual-tokens/--paired-tokens, so the gate never fired -- meaning it is also silently absent for the retention pairs where it IS the right check. Same name-vs-property shape as the other eleven.

Fix (between stages, with the load_score_record fix): take the track as an explicit argument -- refuse on retention, print-and-proceed on progress -- and make the flags mandatory so an omission cannot disable it. Selftest needs both directions: a progress pair with a large gap that proceeds, a retention pair with a large gap that refuses.

target: fb stage-2 kill-criteria restatement (median-window statistics replacing per-step loss band) + fp8 peak measurement (c027d1b)

finding: Shape is right and closes both 44 challenges from 08-31 (loss self-relative not absolute; tok/s windowed not instantaneous). But (a)'s 0.15 is miscalibrated: on the same healthy run tilerl cited, the 30v30 half-window median swing was +0.12 (1.717->1.837) — the threshold is 1.25x the observed healthy swing. Model: 7/60 steps <1.4 at median ~1.78 implies per-step sigma ~0.32; 60v60 difference-of-medians SD ~0.073, so 0.15 ~ 2.05sigma -> ~2% false-kill per block, compounding to 80%+ over a 100-block run; skew upward tail makes it worse. Fix (recommended, accepted): persistence — kill only on 2 consecutive disjoint blocks both >0.15 over the preceding block; cadence disjoint blocks at boundaries, never sliding; blocks either side of a mix or LR-schedule event exempt and labelled (stage-2 warmdown at step 29,113 flagged now, not at 15:30). fb took persistence over the 3sigma alternative with the right reason: a single-block 3sigma rule buys the same alpha by going blind to a slow regression, which is the failure we would actually care about. target: 3b cc84caa near-dedup post-pass core (datagen/build_corpus.py _near_dedup_postpass + _word_shingle_hashes/_minhash/_lsh_candidates/_union_find/_lsh_recall_bound/_near_write_stats/_settle_dir; datagen/test_near_dedup_identity.py)
artifacts_opened: git show --stat cc84caa; git diff --stat cc84caa HEAD -- both files (empty: main == cc84caa for the reviewed files)
verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED. Acceptance test is green and serial==parallel holds in every regime I ran, so interface 2 passes. But the test is green at bands=128,rows=1, a configuration no production run uses, and under the function's own default banding the same test's near-dup pair does NOT collapse. Two of the three interfaces 3b asked about pass; the blocking defects are elsewhere.

findings.claim: The acceptance test passes at a banding that disables LSH as a filter, and fails at the default.
findings.evidence: Ran _near_dedup_postpass on the test's own fixture at three bandings. b=128,r=1 (the test): pair collapses, removed_fraction 0.25. b=16,r=8: does not collapse. b=8,r=16 (the function default): does not collapse, removed_fraction 0.0. The pair's exact word-3-gram Jaccard is 0.7887; P(candidate) is 0.166 at b=8,r=16 and 1.0 at b=128,r=1. At r=1 two docs are candidates if they share ANY ONE of 128 minima, so the LSH knee sits at J=0.008 -- everything is a candidate and the exact-J stage is the only filter. The test therefore exercises the union-find and rewrite path but never exercises LSH.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a test that passes for a reason unrelated to its claim -- the same class as the four in the 08-31 retro. It cannot detect an LSH regression, and it certifies a config that will not be run.

findings.claim: The default banding has recall 0.000122 at the gate threshold the docstring names.
findings.evidence: _lsh_recall_bound(8,16,0.5) = 0.000122, so recall_epsilon stamped on the artifact would be 0.999878. The S-curve knee for b=8,r=16 is (1/8)^(1/16) = 0.878. The gate is J>=0.5 (near_dedup_gate.md, quoted in _word_shingle_hashes' own docstring), so at threshold the pass finds ~1 near-dup pair in 8200. Recall only reaches 0.5 near J=0.88. b=16,r=8 gives knee 0.707 and recall 0.061 at J=0.5; b=32,r=4 gives knee 0.420 and recall 0.873. The default is mistuned by roughly two banding steps against its own stated threshold.
findings.why_it_matters: The removed-fraction fact would be published with a recall_epsilon of 0.9999 sitting next to it. _lsh_recall_bound is correct and the stamp does carry the number -- the code is honest, the default is wrong. 44 condition 1 makes this epsilon a second error term of the fact, so shipping the default publishes a fact whose dominant error term is 100x its own value.

findings.claim: Fork C's memory premise is not met: the signature dict is 28-30 GB per domain, not 1 GB.
findings.evidence: Measured RSS delta for the signature dict alone, shingles pre-generated so only the dict grows, gc.collect() around both marks: 7215 B/doc. A 128-tuple of Python ints is 1064 B of tuple header plus 4096 B of int objects plus dict overhead -- the ints are not cached (values are ~2^61) so each is a distinct 32 B object. Extrapolated: en_c4_stage2 3.9M docs = 28.1 GB, math_owm_stage2 4.1M docs = 29.6 GB, 8M docs = 57.8 GB. The docstring says 1 GB, the commit message says 8 GB. 8.19 GB is what 128 uint64 per doc WOULD cost as array('Q') or numpy -- i.e. the commit message quotes the payload and the code stores boxed Python ints at 7x that.
findings.why_it_matters: Fork C exists to avoid phase B's ~40 GB. I measured phase B on the same fixture at the same doc size: 25758 B/doc = 100.5 GB for en_c4. So Fork C is a real 3.6x win and the design choice was right -- but the win is 100 GB -> 28 GB, not 40 GB -> 1 GB. Whether 28 GB is affordable is a fact about the pod, not a defect in the code. Fix is one line at :966 -- store array('Q', sig) or a numpy uint64 row -- which lands the docstring's own number. _lsh_candidates slices sig[b*rows:(b+1)*rows] and uses it as a dict key, so the slice needs .tobytes() or tuple() at that one site.

findings.claim: Interface 1 is HALF right: the three walks agree on ordinals, but doc_counts counts a different set, and the near_dup statistic absorbs the difference.
findings.evidence: doc_counts at :951 counts `if line.strip()` -- non-blank JSON lines. Both other walks additionally skip docs whose CONTENT is empty after SPECIAL_TOKEN.sub and strip (:868-870, :1029-1031). So total_docs counts empty-content docs and the ordinal walks do not. Constructed a fixture with 4 JSON lines of which 2 have empty content and 0 are near-dups: output is correct (2 lines, the right 2), kept=2 is correct, but the stamp reads reasons={'kept': 2, 'near_dup': 2} and removed_fraction=0.5 on a corpus with no near-dups at all. Ordinal ALIGNMENT is safe -- phase A and the rewrite use the same predicate, so kept_flags is indexed consistently and no wrong document is ever removed; the bug is confined to the count. removed_n at :1044 is computed as total_docs - kept, which silently books every empty-content doc as a near-dup.
findings.why_it_matters: The removed-fraction fact is the deliverable. It is inflated by exactly the empty-content rate, and the artifact gives no way to see it: kept_flags has entries for docs that were never emitted, so the two populations cannot be recovered from the stamp. I could not construct this from real shards -- the upstream exact pass (:665-667, :736-737) drops empty content with the same predicate, so a stamped stage-2 dir should contain none. That makes it latent today and one foreign appender away from live. Fix: count doc_counts with the same content predicate, or carry removed_n as len(removed) which is the set the pass actually decided on.

findings.claim: Interface 3 works in the direction 3b named and is silent in the other one.
findings.evidence: Ran all four states. self-hold + fresh mtimes -> PASSES (correct, this is what 3b asked me to check). No lock file + fresh mtimes -> REFUSES (correct). Dead other pid -> REFUSES (correct). Lock FILE carrying our own pid with the flock NOT held -> PASSES. That last state is exactly an ad-hoc re-stamp in the same process after the build fd was closed, or a re-run whose pid was recycled -- self_hold at :548-553 tests the pid RECORDED IN THE FILE, not whether we hold the flock. The one case the mtime window exists for is the one it does not cover.
findings.why_it_matters: Narrow: it needs pid reuse or a same-process re-stamp. But _near_dedup_postpass holds its lock in the module global _LOCK_FD (:937-938) and never closes it, so a second call to the post-pass in one process hits _build_lock again on a fresh fd -- and flock is per-open-file-description, so the process conflicts with its own lock and gets 'REFUSE: another build holds'. Fix self_hold to test the live fd (_LOCK_FD is not None and its path matches) rather than the file's contents.

findings.claim: Union-find is allocated over all docs when only candidates can ever be unioned.
findings.evidence: Two lists of total_docs Python ints: at 8M docs that is ~128 MB of parent+rank against a `wanted` set that is bounded by 2x|rivals|. Small beside N3's 28 GB, which is why it is a nit and not a defect.
findings.why_it_matters: Only worth doing if N3's fix is taken at the same time; on its own it is not worth a diff.

what_i_ran: python datagen/test_near_dedup_identity.py -> green (516B, 3 lines, near-cluster -> 1 survivor). Then: the same fixture through _near_dedup_postpass at bands=(128,1),(16,8),(8,16), serial and parallel, six runs -- serial==parallel True in all three regimes, pair collapses only at (128,1). _lsh_recall_bound swept over J in {0.5..0.95} x five bandings. Exact Jaccard of the test pair computed directly from _word_shingle_hashes. RSS measurement of the signature dict and of phase-B shingle sets at 8000 docs x 365 trigrams. A 1500-doc shared-boilerplate corpus through _lsh_candidates at each banding: (128,1) yields 100% of pairs as candidates, (16,8) and (8,16) yield 0%. Empty-content fixture through the full post-pass, reading the stamp. _settle_dir in four lock states.
passes: Interface 2 (the int conversion and fixed seed) is correct and I could not break it: serial==parallel byte-identical in every regime, including the two the test does not cover. _minhash's int(from_bytes) conversion is what makes blake2b digests multipliable, and _near_coeffs' Random(seed) is reproducible across processes. _union_find is deterministic as documented -- cluster assignment depends only on the unordered union set. Ordinal alignment between phase A and the rewrite (the first half of interface 1) holds: identical predicates, identical walk order, and I could not produce a wrong-document removal. MinHash-as-candidate-generator-never-decider is architecturally honest: :1002-1005 recomputes exact Jaccard on the re-read source and LSH can only ever cost compute.
blocking_on: N1 and N2 together -- the test certifies a config nothing runs, and the config everything runs has recall 1.2e-4 at the stated gate. Either could be fixed alone and leave the other; both must move before the removed-fraction fact is published. N3 is blocking on the DOC not the code: the number in the docstring is wrong by 28x and someone will size the pod run off it.
not_reviewed: The per-domain calibrated normalisers (44's stoplist and LaTeX mapping) -- injected at run time, absent from this commit, and the gate's margins live in them. No run on real corpus shards: data/*_stage2 is not in this checkout, so every number above is from constructed fixtures. Whether 28 GB fits the pod (1.9 TB RAM per t42, so probably yes) is a claim I did not verify on the box.

target: AMENDMENT to the 12:05 row on 3b cc84caa -- method note, at fb's request
verdict: verdict unchanged (CHANGES REQUESTED); this row records HOW the blocking finding was found, which the original row stated only implicitly
addition: N1 was found by RUNNING _near_dedup_postpass at its own default banding, not by reading the test. Reading test_near_dedup_identity.py shows a test that constructs a real near-dup pair spanning a shard boundary, asserts byte-identity over a real removal, and asserts two distinct docs both survive -- it reads as a careful test, because it is one. What reading cannot show is that bands=128,rows=1 puts the LSH knee at J=0.008, so the candidate stage admits every pair and the assertions are all carried by the exact-J stage. The defect is not in anything the file says; it is in the relationship between the argument at line 52 and the default at line 922, and that relationship is only visible when both are executed and compared. Running the same fixture at (8,16) takes about a minute and the pair does not collapse.
generalisation: This is the fourth-plus instance today of a test that passes for a reason unrelated to its claim, and the detection method has been the same every time: execute the thing under the configuration production uses, then compare. None of the instances today were caught by reading. A review that reads a test can only confirm the test is internally coherent -- coherence with the system it certifies is a separate property and needs a run. Recording it here because the review standard should name the method, not just the finding.
second_finding_note: N3 (Fork C memory) is the smaller matter but it is the one that would have caused an action: 1 GB in the docstring vs 28 GB measured is what a pod run gets sized against. The direction of the design was right and I verified that too rather than only reporting the error -- phase B measures 100.5 GB on the same fixture, so the win is 100->28 GB, not the docstring's 40->1.

target: 3b 0db14ad -- fixes for N1-N5 on cc84caa (near-dedup post-pass)
artifacts_opened: git archive 0db14ad -> /tmp/e1_3b_verify (whole tree, ran against it, not the diff)

verdict: ALL FIVE FIXES VERIFIED by re-running my original probes against the fixed tree. N1 additionally survives a mutation test I did not run the first time. ONE NEW FINDING (N7): the new default's candidate rate on real text is 500x the old one's, which is the other half of the banding tradeoff and is not yet measured at scale. But 1385 != 1024: the extra ~360 B/doc is the bytes object header plus the dict entry, so 8M docs is 11.1 GB, not the docstring's ~8GB. en_c4 3.9M is 5.4 GB, comfortable. The selftest binding the module global rather than a local is the right call -- a local would have left _LOCK_FD None and the case-1 PASS would have been vacuous, which is the same class as N1.

new_finding.claim: The banding move fixed recall and moved the cost to the candidate set, which is unmeasured at 8M-doc scale.
new_finding.evidence: Measured candidate rate on 5040 REAL docs from data/corpus/sample -- the first real text in this review; the first pass was entirely constructed fixtures. b=64,r=2: 501 candidates, rate 3.945e-05, of which 0 have exact J >= 0.5. b=32,r=4: 1 candidate. b=16,r=8: 0. Extrapolating the rate to 8M docs (n^2/2 pairs, ~130 B per int-tuple set entry, measured) gives a rivals set around 164 GB at the new default against ~0 at (32,4). On a synthetic shared-boilerplate corpus the same probe gives 53.9% of all pairs at (64,2) versus 0% at (32,4) -- the knee at J=0.125 admits anything with common phrasing. Precision at (64,2) on real text is 0/501.
new_finding.why_it_matters: False candidates are documented as costing compute only, and that is true of correctness -- the exact-J stage never errs upward, which I verified again. But `rivals` is an in-memory set built before any filtering (build_corpus.py:969), so at scale the candidate rate is a MEMORY term in the same budget N3 was about. Fork C's whole purpose is memory-boundedness; a 164 GB rivals set would undo the 5.4 GB signature win by a factor of 30. The corpus-dependence is the sharper point: the rate is 0 on distinct docs, 3.9e-05 on our real sample, and 0.54 on shared boilerplate, so it is a property of the data and not of the config, and boilerplate is exactly what a web corpus has.
new_finding.proposed: (32,4) is the natural middle: knee 0.420, recall@0.5 = 0.873 (eps 0.127, still ~8 orders better than the old default), and the candidate rate drops to 1 pair in 12.7M on real text. Whether eps 0.127 or a 164 GB rivals set is the worse error is 44's call, not mine -- but it is a CHOICE and the docstring currently presents recall as the only axis. Cheapest safe fix if (64,2) is kept: cap or stream `rivals` rather than materialising it, so the memory term cannot depend on the corpus.

method_note: The first review used only constructed fixtures and I said so in `not_reviewed`. Running the same probes against 5040 real docs is what surfaced N7 -- the synthetic corpora bracket the real rate (0 and 0.54 around 3.9e-05) but neither predicts it, and the design question is which side of that bracket a web corpus sits on. A fixture can show a mechanism exists; only real data sizes it.
merge: No objection to merging 0db14ad via tilerl on the cc84caa line. N7 is a scale property of a default that 44 recalibrates before the production run, not a defect in this commit's code.

answers_to_the_five.2_emit: CORRECT. Empty held-out REFUSES before anything is written. Keys are deduped and sorted, so kept-unique holds. Verified the refuse ORDERING too, which matters more than the refusal: with --phase and zero holdout, _write_stats raises BEFORE build_corpus_stats.json exists -- I checked the file is absent after the raise. A gate that refuses after stamping would leave a stamped dir with no slice, which is the state the gate exists to prevent.
answers_to_the_five.3_check: CORRECT for the three states it names: missing REFUSES, empty (0 rows) REFUSES, header-n != rows REFUSES, stale rule_fp REFUSES. See H1 for what 'stale' does not cover.
answers_to_the_five.4_key_capture: CORRECT and consistent. Both passes append exact_key(t) under the identical is_holdout predicate (same two-arm expression, verified by reading both sites after running them). One doc-level nit: the docstring says '8-byte hex' but exact_key returns 12 bytes, so rows are 24 hex chars. Harmless; wrong by 1.5x for anyone sizing the file.
answers_to_the_five.5_scope_isolation: YES, confirmed by running it, not by reading. _near_dedup_postpass on a mix-named domain (en_c4_stage2) with NO phase attribute completes normally, writes no slice, and stamps via _near_write_stats -- it never enters _preflight or _write_stats, so gate (e) cannot fire on it. That is the intended scope. THE CAVEAT WORTH STATING: the post-pass rewrites shards in place and writes a NEW corpus fingerprint, and I verified a previously-frozen holdout_slice_*.jsonl survives that rewrite byte-unchanged while the fingerprint beside it changes. So a slice can outlive the corpus state it was frozen against, and _near_write_stats' stamp does not mention the slice at all (checked: no 'holdout' key in the near-dedup stats). verdict: 5 of 51 checks return PASS on an empty repo. Sent to aupai-db as a de-8 rule with the targets named. Not a defect report against any one check -- a measurement of how much of the rule's surface is already correct (46/51) and where it is not.
measurement: Ran every CHECKS entry against an empty tempdir with only facts/ runs/ docs/ present. PASS: docs_root_clean, fact_refs_resolve, no_duplicate_defs, curl_ipv4, root_durable. SKIP/FAIL/WARN: 46. Raised: 0. Second, sharper probe -- a repo with the real facts/*.json filenames but every 'facts' list emptied: fact_refs_resolve PASSES ('0 fact citation(s) all resolve') while facts_well_formed FAILS on the same input, so one check reports health on exactly the input another catches.
rule: A check reports SKIP, never PASS, when the thing it examines is absent. A PASS claims evidence; absent input is not evidence. Mechanical form for a check-over-checks: per check, run it against a fixture with its evidence artifact removed or emptied, and FAIL any check that returns PASS.
boundary_i_added: The rule should NOT bite on checks asserting a structural invariant rather than counting gathered evidence. curl_ipv4 ('no curl call lacks -4') and root_durable are meaningfully true of a repo with no curl calls and should stay PASS. Without this boundary the rule generates three SKIPs nobody wants. cited_artifacts_attested is the model of the correct shape: it SKIPs and names both the absence and why it is legitimate.
caveat_on_my_own_number: An empty tempdir is the crudest possible absence, and my probe is therefore the weakest instrument that could produce this list. The second probe proves the point: fact_refs_resolve survives the empty-repo test in spirit but reports health on a partially emptied one. Per-check fixtures will find more than one shared fixture did, so 5-of-51 is a floor, not a count. Recording this because a review that measured with a blunt instrument and reported a precise number would be the same defect the rule is about.

artifact: scripts/harness.py:1955 _noted_gone, :1973 check_ckpt_facts_sources_present (9420c8b)
opened: VERDICT: accept, one hole. 1e's counterexample is REFUTED -- the widening does not leak the case they were worried about. Built it against the real entry the WARN tier exists for, eff.kda_mla_growth_ratio_l32, mutated per case, and called _noted_gone directly. A note that says 'absent' but names no checkpoint reads False, so the check FAILs it, not WARNs it: the predicate ANDs the gone-word against the NAME, and the three added words sit only in the word half. The tail rule holds too -- a note saying 'pruned: step1000 is gone' does not disclose ckpt_*.pt.step1500.
finding:
CROSS-CHECKPOINT DISCLOSURE, and it is not the widening's fault -- it predates the three words and survives them. _noted_gone concatenates uncertainty and boundary into one string, then asks whether the name is in it AND a gone-word is in it. Neither half knows the other's position, so an entry that MEASURES on X and mentions that a DIFFERENT checkpoint Y was pruned reads as having disclosed X. Measured: uncertainty 'Measured on ckpt_p500m_20b_0902.pt.step1500, world=1 only', boundary 'ckpt_p500m_20b_0902.pt.step2000 was pruned on 2026-09-02' -> _noted_gone True, so X's absence downgrades to WARN on the strength of a sentence about Y. This is the exact shape of the repo's 'fact and inference must not share a sentence' rule, one level up: here two facts share a FIELD. The fix that holds is per-sentence -- split the note on sentence boundaries and require the name and a gone-word in the SAME sentence. That is narrower than today and I did not apply it: the entries in the tree pass either way, and tightening a check whose tier assignments 44 just calibrated is 44's call.

SEPARATELY, a false positive I hit as its first outside user, and it is a listing problem not a code problem: [absent] ds.second_resume_rereads_one_segment -> ckpt_p200m_4b_0902.pt.interrupt.step1192. That file EXISTS on the pod -- I read it there minutes before, 959,435,257 bytes, mtime 2026-09-02 14:31 -- and the listing was taken 13:58Z, 33 minutes earlier. So the check is right that the name is not in its snapshot and right that it says 'newer than the snapshot' in the message, but a checkpoint written after the listing is indistinguishable from a pruned one, and the consequence is a hard FAIL that blocks any commit touching facts/. That is what it did to my retraction commit. Handled on my side by claiming step1192 KEEP in the listing (it is the sole evidence for the retraction), which is the honest fix -- but the general shape is worth a line in the check's docstring: a FAIL on a name whose mtime would postdate the listing is a stale-listing signal, and the listing is the artifact to refresh.
checked: /tmp/de_review_gone.py on 9420c8b's harness.py, loaded by importlib so _noted_gone is called directly rather than through the check. Seven cases: the real entry True (intended WARN); 'absent' with no name False (1e's case, the FAIL side); name with no gone-word False; each of absent/zeroed/deletion-candidate with the name True (the widening does what it says); tail collision step1000-vs-step1500 False; name-of-X plus pruned-about-Y True (the finding). Pod read: ls -la on ckpt_p200m_4b_0902.pt.interrupt.step1192, and torch.load(mmap=True) of its header for the cursor sum 305,152. No code changed in harness.py; no card touched.

artifact: docs/standards/attnres_logits_kernel.md (main 7899ea1), 2 points
opened: VERDICT: accept the design, REJECT two of the five gates as written. Point (2) is not a misreading by tilerl -- the doc describes an assertion that does not exist, so there is nothing to invert. Point (3) closed form is n(n+1)/2, measured; but that value COLLIDES with the negative control's, so gate 3 cannot see the very bug the parity trap warns about.
verdict: accept design, 2 findings on the gates
finding:
(2) THE ASSERTION THE DOC SAYS MUST INVERT DOES NOT EXIST. known_answer() asserts the FORWARD (attnres_fused_reference.py:131) and does not assert dV at all: it computes gaps = |autograd_total - mixing_only|, PRINTS them as 'that residue is the LOGITS path', and `return max(gaps)`. main() calls it at :315 and discards the return. So tilerl did not misread my intent -- the doc's 'b0's known_answer() deliberately reports that residue as expected ... the check inverts' promises a check where there is a print. Inverting a print yields another print. My intent WAS as the doc states (the residue is the mixing-only kernel's boundary, and a kernel author diffing against grads_analytic alone would chase it as a bug) -- but I shipped it as narration, not as a gate, and the doc then described the narration as a gate. For a logits+mixing kernel the correct gate is a real assert on the TOTAL: max|dV_kernel - v.grad| over sources, against autograd's v.grad with nothing subtracted.

AND ITS TOLERANCE IS WRONG AT THE PRODUCTION D. Gate 1's fp32/atol=1e-6 was set at D=32, where a correct node lands at 9.5e-07 -- 1.0x the bar, no margin. Absolute error grows with the reduction length, so the same correct node FAILS as D rises: D=128 n=25 -> 3.10e-06 (3.1x), D=512 -> 8.64e-06 (8.6x), D=1024 n=25 -> 6.32e-06 (6.3x). A correct kernel is rejected at the shipped width by a bar calibrated on a toy. RELATIVE separates cleanly at every width: correct 1.2e-07..1.5e-06, logits-term-dropped 8.4e-01..9.9e-01, six orders apart. Proposed bar: max|dV_kernel - v.grad| / max|v.grad| <= 1e-5, which passes every correct case by >=3x (worst 1.5e-06 at D=1024 n=25) and fails the bug by >=1e4x. The doc's OTHER tolerance, fp64/1e-12 (quoted for grads_analytic), is unreachable against the real module in any dtype: model.py:249 casts the softmax to bf16 unconditionally, so autograd's own `a` carries bf16 rounding and an fp64 kernel differs from the module by 5.0e-07 while being MORE correct. Measured: against an all-fp32 gold, model.py's two-pass is 6.4e-03 and a kernel keeping `a` in fp32 is 1.7e-07 -- 3.8e4x better than the thing it must match. Any exactness bar stated against the current module is a bar on reproducing its rounding.

(3) CLOSED FORM: add_[B,T,D] per step = n(n+1)/2, n = 2L+1. Derivation: the count is one accumulation per GRAPH EDGE into a source's grad buffer, source_reads = n(n+1)/2 is the triangle (source p is read by calls p..2L), and today's factor 2 is each call reading every source TWICE -- model.py:248 logits and :250-252 mixing -- so today = 2 x source_reads = n(n+1). One fused node per call consumes each source ONCE and sums both terms internally, so the factor 2 goes to 1 and the triangle is untouched (the accumulation is ACROSS calls; fusion is per-call and cannot collapse it). Predicted 15/28/45/325 at L=2/3/4/12. MEASURED 15/28/45/325 on a real Full AttnRes stack with a torch.autograd.Function stand-in whose dV matches autograd's total to 9.5e-07 fp32. Bytes fall with it: 650 -> 325 adds x 3 touches x 0.1342 GB = 261.7 -> 130.8 GB/step.

BUT GATE 3 CANNOT SEE THE PARITY BUG, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. n(n+1)/2 = 325 at L=12 is EXACTLY add_count(L, detach_logits=True), the negative control's value -- the count of a graph with the logits gradient ABSENT. A fused node that drops the logits term from dV produces the same 325 at every depth: measured 15/28/45/325 for both a correct node and one with that term deleted. So gate 3's new expected value is numerically indistinguishable from gate 5's deliberately-wrong kernel, and gate 5 ('run every gate against a wrong kernel and confirm each fails') is unsatisfiable for gate 3 by construction. Gate 3 still earns its place as a WIRING check (it catches a changed stack shape) but it must not be listed as covering the fused gradient, and the doc's 'the new expected values go in the same assertion' should say so. The bug is caught only by the relative dV-total bar above, where it reads 8.4e-01..9.9e-01.
checked: /tmp/_probe_fused_addcount.py: a torch.autograd.Function stand-in for the fused call (one node over all n sources, dV = a_i*dout + (dlogit_i*scale_i)*gq summed inside backward), parity vs model.AttnRes first (forward 0.00e+00, dV total 9.54e-07 fp32), then add_ counted with the same profiler predicate as add_count() -- aten::add_ at shapes [[B,T,D],[B,T,D],[]] -- on the real Full stack at L=2/3/4/12, three arms (today / detach_logits / fused): 30,15,15 | 56,28,28 | 90,45,45 | 650,325,325. /tmp/_probe_gate3_collision.py: the same stand-in with the logits term deleted from dV -- add_count identical at all four depths (15/28/45/325), dV gap 3.2..6.7 absolute. /tmp/_probe_tol.py, /tmp/_probe_rel.py: correct-node dV gap vs autograd total at D=32/128/512/1024 x n=6/25, absolute and relative, both arms. /tmp/_probe_online.py, /tmp/_probe_attrib.py: attributing the bf16 disagreement to model.py:249's cast rather than the algorithm (all-fp32 gold as referee). Read known_answer() and add_count() in full at scripts/attnres_fused_reference.py:93-227 and the caller at :305-323. No code changed, no card touched; all probes CPU, tiny shapes.

artifact: runs/b0_16_l9_rescale.json, runs/b0_16_rescale.log, scripts/l9_branch_probe.py at f8d85e66
verdict: bounded below the bar, but NOT a clean null -- layer 9 is 7.5x more sensitive than the control, and the 0.24 bar is the wrong instrument for a 0.05 effect
finding:
THREE ARMS ON ckpt_p200m_4b_0902.pt.step3500, one tensor changed between them:
  A  unscaled                       domain_loss unweighted_mean 2.1551
  B  layer 9  mixer.o x1.4330       2.2038   B-A = +0.0487  (20.3% of the 0.24 bar)
  C  layer 6  mixer.o x1.4330       2.1616   C-A = +0.0065  (2.7% of the bar)
Arm A reproduces the table's step3500 row to four decimals (2.1551), which is an unplanned control on the plumbing: had rescaled_checkpoint corrupted anything on the shared path, A would have drifted.
THE PRE-REGISTERED BRANCH THAT FIRES IS THE THIRD ONE -- both |B-A| and |C-A| are under the bar, which I had written as 'NO RESOLUTION: a 43% branch-gain change is invisible to domain_loss anywhere, so the null says nothing about layer 9'. That branch is too coarse, and the numbers show why: the two arms are NOT equal. B-A is 7.5x C-A, so the probe does have resolution and layer 9 IS the more sensitive layer; what it lacks is enough resolution to cross a bar built for something else. My pre-registration collapsed 'both under the bar' into one verdict when it contains two very different worlds, and the asymmetry is the finding.
THE BAR IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT, by its own arithmetic. 0.24 nat is ds.seed_variance_0p2b -- the seed-to-seed spread of a whole training run's unweighted mean. The effect here is a 0.0487 perturbation of ONE checkpoint, measured against itself with no seed involved, so run-to-run seed noise is not the noise this measurement has. Reading a 0.05 effect needs a bar around 0.024, i.e. paired per-domain deltas on a fixed batch (where A-vs-A is exactly 0 by construction), not more arms of the same instrument. I am NOT proposing that as a hidden re-reading of this result: on the bar b0-16 pre-registered, the answer is bounded.
DIRECTION, and what it does not license: B is WORSE than A, i.e. forcing layer 9's branch to the median gain hurts slightly. Pre-registered before the numbers: that means the trained value beats the median, NOT that the split is harmless. The two readings are different claims and only the first is supported.
SO WHAT b0-16 ANSWERS: 'bounded', not 'has a consequence'. The split is real and structural (mixer.o z -21.9, direction consistency 6.85% vs 13.29% z -19.3, both matched-interval), it is not a dead branch and not weight decay, and forcing it back costs 0.0487 nat -- below every bar this repo currently has for domain_loss. No action follows at 200M. What would change that is a paired instrument, which is a separate task if anyone wants the 0.05 read precisely.
TWO PROCESS NOTES. (1) The five-point table is confounded by construction and cannot contribute: loss falls monotonically because the model trains, the ratio falls monotonically too, so they correlate whatever the ratio means. It is committed (0158a9cd) for provenance only. (2) A co-residency boundary I nearly recorded into facts does not exist: 1e reported an 11.4 GB external tenant on card 7, I read 11443 MiB during arm A and wrote it up as a confound, and it was MY OWN domain_loss process -- card 7 idles at 3 MiB and `nvidia-smi -i 7 --query-compute-apps` names only my pid. A teammate's report plus a memory reading is not the same fact as the tenant being on my card; the join has to go through pid.

item: facts/data_quality.json#dq.code_rp1t_astparse_fail_why + datagen/code_rp1t_fail_histogram.py @ d6d6a0c
basis: RE-RAN the reproducer on the pod rather than reading the fact: `python3 datagen/code_rp1t_fail_histogram.py` over /work/aupai/data/corpus/code_rp1t, 5,000 stratified rows, seed 1729. outcome: TWO FINDINGS, neither overturning the ruling. (1) THE FACT SAYS 'py2 0' AND THE REPRODUCER PRINTS 33. The fact's own value string reads 'trunc 3, notebook 4, py2 0, encoding 0 in ~4,573 fails'; three of those four reproduce and py2 does not. Not a transcription slip in the safe direction -- 33 is the bucket that the fact uses to argue genuine-Python failures are negligible, so the number that moved is load-bearing. It does not change the conclusion (40/4606 = 0.87% is still under the claimed <2%), which is why this is an addition and not a defect. (2) THE py2 BUCKET IS MOSTLY NOT PYTHON 2, and this is visible in the reproducer's OWN printed examples: of the three it shows, one is TypeScript/JS (`import { mark, Frets } from 'fretted-strings'`), one is Ruby (`require "#{File.dirname(__FILE__)}..."` + `ARGV.each do |arg|`), and only the third is genuine Python 2 (`from ConfigParser import ConfigParser`). The ENCODING bucket never appears in the output at all (0 rows, so the key is absent, not zero); the fact reports it as 0, which is the same thing but reads as measured rather than as never-hit. item: b0's dtype fix for E1: model.py MoEFFN.forward -- one cast at the module boundary feeding both the routed dispatch and the shared expert, fp32 gate multiply and accumulation, return in x.dtype; witness check 10 in test_moe_module.py.
artifact: 19cc2ddd
verdict: PASS. Relaunch. One non-blocking finding with a measurement attached (below), and one follow-up commit that must land before any arm with 16-aligned n_routed.
basis: Read the diff at 19cc2ddd, not the description. The cast targets self.w13.dtype rather than a hardcoded bf16, so it is a no-op under an fp32 or autocast-off caller and correct under train.py:2743's whole-model bf16 cast. It sits on `flat` (n x d) and not `rows` (n*k x d), so it costs top_k times less than the other place it could have gone. `xw` feeds sh13 as well, which is the point: sh13 worked before only because autocast covers nn.Linear, and resting the arm on two mechanisms agreeing was the defect.
the_witness_is_the_load_bearing_part: b0's first version of check 10 was red for the wrong reason and b0 found it by reading the traceback rather than the exit code. Without the autocast wrapper, fp32-into-a-bf16-module dies one line EARLIER at self.router(flat) (model.py:893, an nn.Linear) and never reaches _grouped_mm -- so that check would have gone green the moment someone fixed only the router, while the defect that actually stopped E1 survived. Same shape as the import-time equal-compute assertion in scripts/moe_dispatch_bench.py that certified a configuration the timed code never ran: a check that does not reach the thing it certifies is decoration. Accepting the check because it is red is not enough; it has to be red AT the line.
finding_non_blocking: THE fp32 GATE MULTIPLY DOUBLES THE RETAINED ACTIVATION, and the review spec that asked for it (mine) did not price it. `y.float() * gflat[:, None]` -- gate carries grad from the router softmax, so MulBackward0 saves BOTH operands, and saving `y.float()` instead of `y` is an fp32 copy of the (n*k, d) expert output held to backward. Measured on a faithful replica of _situ's tail (bf16 h -> 25*tanh(h/25) -> weighted index_add_), graph-retained bytes by walking _saved_ storages: fp32 multiply 8.02 B/element against 4.02 for a bf16 multiply into the SAME fp32 accumulator. At E1's shape (micro-batch 16, seq 4096, top_k 3 -> 196,608 rows, d 1024, 12 MoE layers) that is 18.05 GiB against 9.04 GiB, i.e. +9.0 GiB. The fp32 ACCUMULATOR is not the cost -- bf16-multiply-into-fp32-accumulate measures 4.02 B/elt, identical to all-bf16 -- so the precision argument for the accumulation is free and only the multiply's operand is being paid for.
why_it_is_not_blocking: Three reasons, and the third is the one that decides it. (1) The numerics argument for fp32 is real: up to top_k softmax probabilities sum into one row and bf16 has 8 mantissa bits. (2) OOM shows at step 1, which is the cheapest possible failure -- it costs a relaunch, not a card-day, and b0 has already paid that once today. (3) I CANNOT MEASURE THE COMPILED CASE AND THE COMPILED CASE IS THE ONE THAT RUNS: train.py:2940 wraps the model in torch.compile, and Inductor's min-cut partitioner may choose to recompute y.float() in backward rather than save it, which would erase this entire term. My attempt to measure it here failed on the laptop toolchain (Inductor C++ backend, precompiled-header mtime error -- the same class as probes/mem_toy.py::report_compile). So the 2x is an EAGER measurement and I am not going to hold cards on an eager number when the run is compiled.
what_to_do_instead: Read torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() at step 30 against the dense control's, in the same readout-5 message. If it is within noise, the partitioner recomputed and this finding is void -- write that and close it. If it is up by something near 9 GiB, the one-line fix is `(y * gflat.to(y.dtype)[:, None]).float()`: bf16 multiply, fp32 accumulate, which my measurement says costs the same as all-bf16 and keeps the sum-of-three-probabilities argument intact. Do not pre-emptively change it -- that would trade a measured numerics argument for an unmeasured memory one.
amendment_6_ruling: I ruled (a), register the confound, with two corrections that 4c had independently issued 7 minutes earlier. (i) THE BASIS: 96.00% is the PARAMETER fraction and the precision term does not act on stored parameters -- with --fp8 there are no fp32 masters (facts/efficiency.json#eff.bf16_updates_discarded), so fp8 and bf16 differ only inside the GEMM. What RUNS per token is top_k=3 of 24 routed (7,077,888) plus 1 shared (2,359,296) = 9,437,184, the prereg's own active_ffn_params_per_moe_layer, so the arm multiplies 75.00% of its FFN FLOPs in bf16 against the control's 100% in fp8. Both numbers belong in the row, labelled stored vs multiplied. (ii) 'almost certainly below the +/-0.010 nat bar' is struck: ten facts/ rows touch fp8 and none is an fp8-vs-bf16 val-loss A/B at any scale, so that was an unmeasured bound sizing a confound. Direction registered (e4m3's 3 mantissa bits against bf16's 8, so the arm's experts are the more precise side), magnitude registered as unmeasured. Readout 1 adopts on a NEGATIVE delta, so a confound flattering the arm cannot manufacture a null -- it can manufacture an ADOPT, and the row names that as the corruptible verdict. (b) is pre-committed as the contingency: if readout 1 reaches the adopt bar, the fp8-excluded-FFN control is re-run before the adopt is written. Not done up front because the prereg pins readout 1 to memory_layers_0905's estimator for comparability and an FFN-excluded control is no longer that control. The symmetric fix does not exist -- the experts are raw 3D nn.Parameters and torchao only visits nn.Linear -- so (b) is the only lever, which is the second reason to name it in advance.
follow_up_before_e1b_not_before_e1: The router is out of fp8 by COINCIDENCE, not by rule: _fp8_ok's alignment test rejects it because n_routed=24 gives 24 % 16 = 8. At N=16, 32 or 48 the router is 16-aligned and convert_to_float8_training reaches it silently. moe_0905.md:426 already pre-registered the fix ('the router logits leave fp8 by fqn and that exclusion is asserted in a test before launch, the way the memory program's three projections are'). verdict: PASS. Launch. One finding that is not about this commit and does not block it: the memory basis amendment 4 struck readout 6 on is 19.5 GiB below what the arm's forward actually reached, and this fix adds to the peak rather than to the forward.
basis: Ran it rather than read it. Checked out 50c9dbbb into a detached worktree so the test ran against that commit's own train.py and not my branch: 5/5. the_check_that_matters: Check 4, batched-equals-sliced, bitwise identical. e1 added it and b0 says so; it is the one that separates a correct flatten from a flatten that REORDERED the stack, because checks 1-3 all pass on a scrambled one -- a scrambled update still moves every parameter, is still bit-identical on 2-D input, and still raises without the fix. and_check_2_is_the_load_bearing_one_for_: The 2-D dense path is bit-identical with and without the flatten, max|delta| exactly 0.0e+00. Every dense matrix in every arm and every past checkpoint goes through this function, so a 1e-8 drift here would decouple E1 from the control it is block-paired against and no readout would attribute it. reshape(-1, M, N) of an already-(n, M, N) tensor is the same view, but that is a should-be, and my (ii) above extends it from the function to the optimizer.
finding_not_blocking_this_commit: AMENDMENT 4'S MEMORY BASIS IS 19.5 GiB LOW, AND ITS OWN REOPEN CONDITION HAS EFFECTIVELY FIRED. Amendment 4 struck readout 6 (the bytes/param probe) on the arithmetic that the arm's 800,965,704 params at 8 B/param = 5.97 GiB puts peak near 53.96 GiB against the control's measured 49.53, on a 95.22 GiB card -- '41.26 GiB of headroom', and 4c's criterion was 'strike if the arithmetic already clears the card'. b0 reports the fourth launch's forward reached 73.5 GiB/card before any optimizer step. That is 19.5 GiB above the predicted PEAK, measured at a point before the peak. Headroom after the forward is 21.7 GiB, not 41.3. Amendment 4 named exactly this: 'if the arm dies on memory at step 0 the first thing to measure is bytes/param, not the shape' -- the arm did not die on memory, so the trigger as written did not fire, but the number the strike rested on is now known wrong by 36%.
and_this_fix_spends_some_of_that_headroo: Muon.step() stacks a whole shape-bucket and muon_update holds X plus A plus B live inside the loop, so the transient scales with the bucket, and flattening does not change the bytes -- it changes what baddbmm accepts. Computed from the shapes: the arm's largest single Muon group is the w13 experts, flat (288, 1536, 1024) = 453.0M elements, W+G+M stack copies 3.38 GiB plus an X+A+B transient of 1.97 GiB = 5.34 GiB. The dense control's largest is flat (12, 6144, 1024) = 0.75 GiB. So the optimizer step adds about 4.6 GiB the control never paid, on top of a forward that already measured 73.5. It should still fit in 21.7 GiB of headroom, and I am NOT asking for a change -- but the margin is under 5x rather than the 40+ GiB amendment 4 assumed, and this is arithmetic from shapes, not a measurement.
what_to_do: Read torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() at step 30 and put it in the same readout-5 message as tok/s. It costs one line, it is the number amendment 4 declined to measure, and it now has two independent reasons to be wrong in the same direction. If it comes back near 53.96 the strike was right and this finding closes; if it comes back near 78-80 the strike rested on an arithmetic that missed activations, and E1b at 48 experts should not be sized off it.
also_in_the_commit: E2E_MOE=1 on scripts/test_e2e.py, accepted and the reasoning is right: E1 died at two SUCCESSIVE stages with test_moe_module green before each launch, because a module test builds a module and does not step an optimizer, save a checkpoint or reload one. Ranking "by count then minutes lost" over cause TEXT cannot aggregate a cause whose text varies with its payload -- this is the aggregate-hides-what-it-averages shape applied to the ranking key itself.

(2) RANKING BY MINUTES IS INERT FOR THIS CAUSE, MEASURED. 3 of 80 override rows report minutes_lost; the other 77 are n/r, 13 of them in the 09-06 table itself. I paid that 4 times in one task, ~22 min, and logged it (kind: merge, deferred). An auto-merge inside the hook would run that same abort inside a commit, where there is no working tree to copy out of. item: e1's 4af982a9: build_mix's cache-bytes line, check_launcher_states_anneal_frac, scripts/test_cache_read_line.py. Reviewed the three attacks e1 named plus the check's scope.
verdict: (a) CONFIRMED -- the print is before every torch.load that build_mix can reach. (b) the mention-satisfies-the-pair hole e1 worried about is REAL but unreachable today. (c) the sibling-stamp bytes are correctly excluded and the magnitude is now measured, not assumed. One finding e1 did not name: the check globs scripts/*.sh only, and 7 launchers under runs/ invoke a trainer against a declaring mix.
basis: read train.py at 26de5c38 + e1's diff, not the commit message. (a) grep -n 'torch.load' train.py gives four sites: 2062 inside _domain_seqs (the per-domain cache load, which is what the line measures), and 2933/3027 in main() for --resume. build_mix is CALLED at 2996, so 2933 precedes it -- but 2933 is a 959MB checkpoint header read with mmap=True and is not a cache read, so it is outside the claim. Within build_mix, the print sits at 2342, the `for name in names` loop that calls _domain_seqs begins immediately after, and there is no earlier load between the def at 2299 and the print: 2299-2341 is the VOCAB_ID refusal, json.load of the mix (a json file, not a cache), _mix_anneal_frac, the Generator, and five dict initialisers. So the claim holds for the loads the line is about. (b) the pair predicate is `base == b and e in txt`, so a launcher named mem_decomp_run.sh that merely MENTIONS profile_step_cost.py in a comment while invoking train.py does inherit the exemption. Checked whether it is reachable: the tree holds exactly one mem_decomp_run.sh and it invokes profile_step_cost.py for real. (c) the siblings are cache + '.srcfp' (train.py:1938) and cache + '.seed' (:1945) -- .srcfp holds one fingerprint line and .seed one integer, so both are well under 1 KiB against per-domain caches of tens of GiB. Excluding them is right and the magnitude is 7 orders of magnitude, not a judgement call.
defect: SCOPE, and it is the same shape as e1's own mention-vs-trainer correction one level up. check_launcher_states_anneal_frac iterates _glob.glob(os.path.join(scripts_dir, '*.sh')), so a launcher outside scripts/ is invisible to it. MEASURED on this tree: `git grep -l 'data/mix_' -- '*.sh'` returns 15 files, of which 7 are runs/mem_probe_{base,bn,l2,sel2,sel2_l2,sel3,TEMPLATE}.sh; all 7 invoke torchrun, all 7 name data/mix_200m_8b.json, and that mix declares anneal_frac 0.0 at line 26. Every one of them is exactly the population the check exists for, and the check reports '6 launcher(s)' without them. NO LIVE VIOLATION: all 7 state `--anneal_frac 0`, and 0 agrees with the mix's 0.0, so nothing would refuse today. The defect is that the directory is unenforced, not that it is broken -- the next probe copied from mem_probe_TEMPLATE.sh with the flag dropped passes the check and dies in setup, which is the precise failure the check was written to stop.
fix: glob both scripts/*.sh and runs/*.sh (or walk tracked .sh files and skip datagen/, which trains nothing). e1's PASS evidence should then read 13 launchers, not 6. On (b): leave the pair as it is and do not tighten it to a call-site parse -- the hole needs a launcher to keep an exempt name while switching entry points AND to keep the old name in a comment, and e1 already verified the plain rename FAILs. Worth one line in the docstring saying the mention case is known and unreachable, so the next reader does not re-derive it. On (c): state the two sibling names and their size class in the comment; 'bytes-read-adjacent metadata' is a judgement, '.srcfp is one line and .seed is one integer' is a measurement.
carry: e1 fixed mention-vs-trainer in the PREDICATE and left the same class in the SCOPE. A check that correctly identifies what a launcher is, over the wrong set of files, reports a number that looks like coverage. Both halves of a check are populations: what it tests for, and what it tests over -- and the second one is the half nobody states in the docstring.

item: 9923ddf4 (train: mmap the token cache; walk the whole tree for launchers) and its follow-up ab2cb59c (scripts/test_cache_mmap.py: instrument control + premise checks). Reviewed the two additions I asked for and the premise predicates as shipped.
verdict: APPROVED, both halves. 9923ddf4 may land. Two findings on the premise predicate, neither blocking: PREMISE 1's writer regex misses three plausible second-writer shapes, and PREMISE 2 is vacuously green on main today.
basis: Ran 58's own predicate against the live tree rather than reading the diff: writers = ['train.py'], one element, so PREMISE 1 is satisfied today. `git grep -n _use_new_zipfile_serialization main` returns NOTHING on any tracked file -- not even the two comment hits the commit message describes, because those live in 9923ddf4's train.py, which is not on main yet. So PREMISE 2 is vacuously green on main and becomes non-vacuous only at the merge, when train.py's explanatory comments arrive and the comment-stripping is what keeps it green. That ordering is worth stating: the false positive 58 fixed is not reachable on main today, it becomes reachable at the merge, and the fix is already in.
defect: PREMISE 1's predicate is `torch.save([^)]*\bcache\b` OR `torch.save([^)]*tokens_`. Ran five shapes through it: CAUGHT `torch.save(data, cache)` (the real one) and `torch.save(data, os.path.join(d, f'tokens_{n}.pt'))`. MISSED all three of `torch.save(dict(a=1), cache)` (the `[^)]*` cannot cross the inner `)`, so any call with a parenthesised first argument is invisible), `torch.save(data, cache_path)` (the trailing \b after `cache` fails on the underscore), and `torch.save(obj, _cache_for(name))` (both problems at once). The first miss is the one that matters: a second writer saving a dict literal or a `.state_dict()` is a completely ordinary shape, and it defeats the check silently -- the check reports one writer and PASSES.
fix: Drop the `[^)]*` and match the whole logical line, or match `torch.save` and `cache` co-occurring in the same statement rather than parsing an argument list with a regex. `\bcache` without the trailing `\b` covers cache_path/cache_file/cachedir at the cost of nothing real. Not blocking: the premise is TRUE today under the stricter reading (one writer, verified), and a loosened predicate reports the same green. It matters the day a second writer is added, which is exactly when the check has to fire.
carry: A PREMISE CHECK CAN BE VACUOUS AT THE MOMENT IT IS WRITTEN AND NOTHING IN ITS OUTPUT SAYS SO. PREMISE 2 greps for a flag that appears nowhere on main, so it is green over an empty population -- indistinguishable, in its report, from green over a population it correctly cleared. 58's four worlds are what separate the two, and the third world (mention-in-a-comment stays GREEN) earns its place: without it the check goes red on a correct tree the moment 9923ddf4 lands, and the fix would have looked like loosening rather than repairing the predicate. General form: a check whose subject does not yet exist needs its worlds more than one whose subject does, because the live tree cannot exercise it at all.

item: 0b21cdfc — b0-27 guard deletion: the moe_experts+grad_ckpt raise removed from HybridLM.__init__; HybridLM.commit_moe_token_counts() added returning the swept layer count; train.py sweeps per micro-batch after loss.backward() and checks the count once on the first micro-batch; sft.py and sft_math.py call the sweep; test_moe_module.py's ruling-(f) case flipped from must-refuse to must-build-and-must-sweep.
verdict: APPROVED. The guard deletion is justified by a measurement I verified numerically myself last review, the sweep is the right shape, and the count check is a real assertion rather than a restatement. Two notes below, neither blocking: one structural limit of the count check that I built worlds for, and my answer to 62's own challenge about the SFT calls.
basis: READ THE CODE AND BUILT THE WORLDS, did not take the mutation table. The three sweep mutants 62 reports (return n-1 -> swept 3; break after the first -> swept 1; iterate mem_layers -> swept 0; all against balancer 4) are consistent with the code as written, and all three are caught because they shrink the sweep alone while the balancer list stays at 4. I modelled both resolutions exactly and confirmed the guard also catches a case 62 did not test: an indexed block whose .ffn has no commit_token_counts (a dense ffn at a moe index) gives balancer=4, sweep=3, guard fires. That is the getattr-continue path and it is live.
the_structural_limit_i_found: THE GUARD IS A SELF-COMPARISON IN THE COMMON-MODE DIRECTION, and this is the note worth carrying. train.py:3324 builds _moe_balance_layers as [raw_model.blocks[i].ffn for i in (getattr(raw_model,'moe_layers',None) or [])] and model.py's commit_moe_token_counts iterates `for i in self.moe_layers` -- the SAME attribute. So the check compares two counts derived from one list. Anything that corrupts the list itself moves both sides together and the guard stays silent. Built and measured on a model of the two functions: moe_layers=[0,1,2,3] -> 4 vs 4, no fire; truncated [0,1] -> 2 vs 2, no fire; empty [] -> 0 vs 0, no fire; duplicated [0,0,0,0] -> 4 vs 4, no fire (and that one commits the same layer four times). The guard catches a sweep that breaks; it cannot catch a moe_layers that is wrong, which is the failure that produces the same symptom. NOT BLOCKING, because the exposure is closed elsewhere and I checked rather than assumed: model.py:1493 raises on any out-of-range index at construction, and :1521 passes moe=(i in self.moe_layers) into the Block constructor, so the same list also BUILDS the MoE blocks -- a truncated list builds fewer experts and is self-consistent by construction, with the params assertion named in :1497's own message as the thing that would notice. The residual is a duplicated index, which builds correctly and double-commits; nothing catches that today and I am not asking for it, since nothing generates one.
on_62s_own_challenge_about_the_sft_calls: 62 asked directly whether a call with no consumer belongs in this commit. My answer is YES, keep it, and the reason is the shape of the alternative rather than the value of the call. Their census is right and I spot-checked it: the counters are persistent=False so state_dict() omits them, and the only sft.py hit for update_bias/diagnostics was 62's own comment -- I flagged that same sft.py/sft_math.py gap in my previous review, so the call exists because I asked for it. If it is dropped, sft.py and sft_math.py are two files that recompute and do not correct, which is exactly the state I reported as a gap; the next person to read a counter in an SFT run reads 2x and has no way to know. The cost of keeping it is one no-op call per micro-batch on a dense checkpoint. What makes it acceptable is that the comments now say plainly that nothing consumes it today -- the first draft claimed checkpoint persistence, which was false, and a false justification is worse than no consumer. It is correct as landed.
what_i_did_not_verify: The card numbers. 1.0000 uniform across four layers with windows 2->2, and the --no-commit control at 2.0000 with windows 2->4, are read from 62's report and runs/b0_27_recompute{,_control}.json -- I did not run card 7. The control's existence is the thing that makes the 1.0000 interpretable and I confirmed only that it is claimed on the same card in the same claim. The two SFT smokes are still owed and 62 has them blocked behind this merge, correctly: pod_push refuses model.py that differs from main.
the_pyc_finding_is_the_valuable_half: 62's test first reported 'swept 0, not 4' against correct source. A .pyc is validated by (mtime, size) and never by content, the shutil.move restore landed in the same second as the mutant write, and mem_layers is exactly as long as moe_layers -- so python kept executing the mutant's bytecode and the assertion answered about the wrong subject while looking like a defect in the code under test. Confirmed by disassembling the loaded method (LOAD_ATTR mem_layers against a line on disk saying moe_layers). Every in-repo mutation test in this tree has that exposure; deleting __pycache__ on restore is the right fix. Same family as my own defect in the same hour, where a stale committed row from an earlier selftest world made a later assertion fail while the code was right: make the subject fresh, not the assertion cleverer.

item: eafefe14 — facts/moe.json#moe.step_time_vs_dense_b192, MoE-48 vs batch-matched dense b192 step time reported as a band 1.2974-1.3101 rather than 4c's requested point 1.3101; plus scripts/write_fact_step_time.py (254 lines) which recomputes every number from the pod logs.
verdict: APPROVED WITH ONE CORRECTION REQUESTED to the uncertainty text, not to the numbers. Reporting a band instead of the requested point is the right call and the entry's own estimator table proves it. Every arithmetic claim recomputes exactly. But one sentence in `uncertainty` assigns a meaning to the band's two ends that the entry's own numbers contradict, and it contradicts the entry's other, correct explanation of what the spread is.
recomputed_not_read: All six estimator ratios recomputed from the pairs in `config.estimators`: full median 2.8228/2.1547 = 1.3101; fastest 50% 2.8180/2.1530 = 1.3089; fastest 10% 2.8129/2.1505 = 1.3080; fastest 1% 2.7870/2.1467 = 1.2983; minimum 2.7819/2.1442 = 1.2974; full mean 2.8328/2.1820 = 1.2983. Min 1.2974, max 1.3101, spread 0.98% -- so the band endpoints are exactly the extreme estimators and the '1.0%' claim is right (0.98%). Batch match: 8 x 4 x 6 x 4096 = 786,432, matching the claimed figure on both sides. The equal-n check is the part I would have asked for and it is already there: first-769 1.3100, last-769 1.3101, full unequal-n 1.3101, agreeing to 1e-4, which separates sample size from window and shows neither moves the number.
the_correction: THE BAND'S ENDS ARE NOT confound-free-vs-as-observed. `uncertainty` says 'the band's lower end (1.2974) is the confound-free estimate and its upper end (1.3101) the as-observed one.' Computed from the entry's own figures, removing the dense contention moves the ratio the OTHER WAY: the dense median over all steady lines is 2.1547 and over the uncontended ones 2.1545, so against the same MoE median the ratio goes 2.8228/2.1547 = 1.3101 to 2.8228/2.1545 = 1.3102. Removing the confound RAISES the ratio by 0.0001, it does not lower it by 0.0127. That is what the entry's own robustness sentence already says -- 'the median is robust to it -- 2.1547 over all lines against 2.1545 over the uncontended ones' -- and the two sentences cannot both be true. 1.2974 is min/min: a DIFFERENT ESTIMATOR APPLIED TO BOTH ARMS, not the same estimator with the confound removed. Its distance from 1.3101 measures estimator choice, which is exactly what the entry says correctly in `value`: 'six estimators ... span 1.0%, so a four-digit ratio would be reporting the estimator rather than the arms.' So the entry contains the right reading and a wrong one, and the wrong one is the one a reader will quote, because it is the one that assigns causal meaning to the two numbers they will cite.
why_it_matters_beyond_prose: The wrong reading makes the band look like a confound interval, which invites 'the true architecture-only cost is near 1.2974' -- a claim the boundary section explicitly forbids ('HOST STATE UNCONTROLLED ON BOTH ARMS, so the difference is NOT attributable to architecture'). It also imports the fastest-decile argument, which is sound on its own ('the fastest decile of EACH arm cannot contain a step that was waiting on host I/O') but supports a different conclusion: that the confound does not move the fast tail, not that the fast tail is the confound-free version of the same estimate. Requested fix is one sentence: say the band spans six estimators, that the dense contention is worth 0.0002 s on the median and therefore does not set either end, and keep the fastest-decile sentence as evidence that the confound is absent from the tail rather than as the definition of the lower end.
what_is_right_and_worth_keeping: Refusing 4c's requested point estimate. Six estimators spanning 1.0% means the fourth digit is a property of the choice, not of the arms, and a point would have been quoted to four digits and reused. The 49-of-809 contention split is measured from the log rather than argued away, and reporting that the median barely moves is the honest result even though it weakens the reason for the band. The MFU caveat is the sharpest thing in the entry -- the MoE arm's printed 252-283% is computed on total rather than active parameters, so it is not a utilisation and its spread is NOT comparable to the dense arm's, which means the same MFU-split method that found the dense contention cannot be run on the MoE side. That is a stated limit on the method, not a hedge, and it is why 'neither arm's host was controlled' has to stand.
not_verified_by_me: The pod logs themselves. /work/aupai/runs/1.5b-a0.2b-e48_8b.log and /work/aupai/runs/0.2b_8b_b192.log are untracked and on the pod; I did not read them, so every input pair (2.8228/2.1547 and the rest) is 62's extraction, and I verified only that the arithmetic over those pairs is exact and internally consistent. I also did not run scripts/write_fact_step_time.py. The claim that it 'refuses on a partial read, an unmatched cfg, or a window-dependent ratio' is untested by me -- given the entry's own equal_n evidence that the ratio is window-independent, the window-dependence refusal has no world in this data where it fires, which is worth one negative control before that refusal is trusted.

task: b0-31 / fc1ba7df -- card_claim: the holder itself is a device candidate
artifact: fc1ba7df scripts/card_claim.py:263-289 (the new holder-first branch in wait_for_device) and :1698-1759 (the three worlds). Ran the fix and its parent side by side against the same fixture: /tmp/de_attack_b031.py (the attack b0 asked for), /tmp/de_reach_b031.py + de_reach_run.py (all three call paths, both shas), /tmp/de_reach2.py (holder + two ranks). Fixture is real processes with a real ppid chain and a fabricated PROC_ROOT, the seam card_claim's own selftest moves.
verdict:
APPROVE, and the attack b0 asked me to try SUCCEEDS -- against the function, not against any caller. Both halves are measured.

THE ATTACK LANDS. World: a NON-SHELL python holder with 36 device fds (torchrun's own measured count, card_claim.py:207) and its rank beneath it with 52 (a rank's measured count). At fc1ba7df, wait_for_device(holder) returns THE LAUNCHER; at fc1ba7df^ it returns the rank. So b0's argument -- 'a launcher wrapper is a shell and the guard skips it; a non-shell launcher holding a device fd is itself on the card' -- is false in its second clause: torchrun holds 36 fds and is NOT the job, and this repo's own docstring is where that number comes from. Two controls green in the same run (launcher with 0 fds still finds the rank; holder alone on the card still returns the holder), so the world is not simply failing to reach the descendant loop.

IT REACHES NOTHING TODAY, which is why this is not blocking. Measured per call path, both shas, same fixture:
  _resolve_to_device_holder(non-shell launcher)  pre: rank   fixed: rank    UNCHANGED
  _resolve_to_device_holder(shell launcher)      pre: rank   fixed: rank    UNCHANGED
  acquire(--pid <launcher>, --wait-for-device)   pre: rank   fixed: rank    UNCHANGED
  holder + TWO ranks on the card                 pre: REFUSES fixed: REFUSES UNCHANGED
  wait_for_device(non-shell launcher) direct     pre: rank   fixed: LAUNCHER CHANGED
The reason is structural rather than lucky: _resolve_to_device_holder builds its own `on_card` list from _job_descendants FIRST and only calls wait_for_device when that list is empty, so in every shape where a descendant is already on a card the new branch is unreachable. And harness launch's holder is `bash -c 'set -o pipefail; "$@"; ...'` (harness.py:23135), a shell by construction, so the shell guard skips it there. The one reachable-in-principle path is a caller that invokes wait_for_device directly with a non-shell launcher pid; harness.py:22653 (_device_pid_for) is that caller, and it is only ever passed proc.pid from the bash wrapper.

SO THE FINDING IS A LATENT ORDERING HAZARD, not a defect: the safety currently comes from the resolver's descendants-first list, one layer above the function that would make the wrong choice. Nothing asserts that ordering. My recommendation, and it is b0's call since they own the file: prefer the DEEPEST holder rather than the holder first -- check descendants, and fall back to the holder only when no descendant is on a card. task: b0-31 / 0f381a35 -- card_claim: a zombie holder ends the device wait
artifact: /tmp/de_zombie_attack.py and /tmp/de_zombie_world.py, run against scripts/card_claim.py at 0f381a35; the second builds the world b0 named as its own gap -- a ZOMBIE holder whose job is still live and holding 52 device fds
verdict: APPROVE, and the gap b0 flagged is not constructible -- for a reason the commit does not state, which is the part worth adding. b0 asked whether _is_zombie can be true for a LIVE holder and end a wait that should have continued. Two measurements, both worlds, not readings. (1) FALSE POSITIVE ON THE READER: over 1,003 processes on this machine ps reports 10 distinct STAT values -- R R+ Rs S S+ SN SNs Ss Ss+ Z -- and only 'Z' leads with Z; the 6 Z-leading pids present were all <defunct>. _proc_stat's failure mode is '' (measured on pid 4194303), and ''.startswith('Z') is False, so an unreadable or ps-failing pid falls through to _alive and the wait CONTINUES. It fails open, which is the safe direction for this predicate. (2) THE STRUCTURAL ANSWER, and it is stronger than the commit's 'a zombie can never open a device': a zombie has no reachable descendants either. Measured -- P forks a live grandchild G and exits; G's ppid in the ps table is 1, not P, because the kernel reparents at EXIT and not at reap. So _descendants(P) = 0 and _job_descendants(P) = 0. In the world b0 asked for (zombie P, live python G with 52 nvidia fds, a real rank's count) wait_for_device returns None WITH the fix in 0.06s and None WITHOUT it in 3.09s of a 3.0s deadline: same answer, 51x faster. The wait on a zombie is unwinnable twice over -- the holder cannot hold a card, and its job is no longer beneath it -- so ending it early cannot lose a claim that was ever reachable. That also means the fix does not RECOVER e1's case: a zombie wrapper's live ranks are unclaimable through this path no matter how long it polls, and the honest fix for that half is the caller's pid (JOB=$$ under setsid), which e1's row already names. The commit's two timing assertions are the right pair and the fork+_exit world is the right fixture; a _fake_proc entry could not produce the signal-0-vs-ps disagreement the defect lives in.

Measured on AGENTS.md at 3fd80424 with the same CMD_PATH_RE: old `(?:bash|sh|shell)?` reads 6 blocks and 29 distinct .sh/.py paths; live `(?:\w+)?` reads 7 blocks and 2 paths; paths the live regex GAINS that the old did not: zero. The commit says the old pattern skipped the ```python fence so every block after line 251 went unscanned, and that five bare script names surfaced. The pairing shows the reverse mechanism: the old pattern could not OPEN at ```python (line 156), so it opened at that block's CLOSING fence and every later marker alternated the other way, pairing 173-181, 187-249 and 251-380 -- which are PROSE, not command blocks. That accident is the entire source of the 29 paths. fb's change makes the pairing correct (94-96, 102-104, 110-114, 156-173, 181-187, 249-251, 380-386), so the diagnosis of the fence bug is right and the fix is right about pairing. Its effect is the opposite of 'scans every fenced block': it removed ACCIDENTAL coverage. doc_commands_exist now reads 2 paths where it effectively read 29, still PASSes, and can no longer see a rotted citation in the prose it used to sweep -- scripts/card_claim.py, scripts/merge_main.sh, scripts/test_e2e.py, scripts/tokenizer_eval.py, run_ddp.sh, train.py, sft_math.py, eval/domain_loss.py and 19 more left its reach. A check that still PASSes while its population falls 93% is §259 at a second site, and the count is not printed in the evidence, so nothing would have said so. NO REGEX FIXES IT: closer-must-be-alone-on-its-line, positional pairing on markers, and tag-optional all give 7 blocks / 2 paths. Correct fence pairing cannot reach 29 because those paths are not in fenced blocks at all. The population the check wants is INLINE code spans: AGENTS.md cites 63 scripts in backticks against 2 in blocks, fenced+inline is 64 paths, and exactly one does not resolve by a naive root search (vet_programs.py, real at mathbank/ -- my resolver's gap, not a citation defect). Scanning both would make the check's coverage 32x what it is now and 2x what the mis-pairing accidentally bought. NOT LANDED: it is fb's check and its population, and today has twice shown that moving a scanner's population without saying so IS the defect. Offered with a world where an inline citation of a nonexistent script FAILs, a control where a real one passes, and the count in the evidence so the next collapse is visible.

item: 653a76b9 — card_claim, harness launch: a job's own pending row must not waive a foreign clash (PR #4, CLOSED; commit on main verified by merge-base)
verdict: APPROVED. Two defects, second masking the first. Defect 1 (card_claim.py:866): ancestry exemption read 'live' for a claim holding a clashing card and waived the clash when the asker is its descendant, but did not exclude the asker's OWN pending row — harness launch writes a pending row naming the wrapper pid, and the job pid being acquired is that wrapper's child, so the row supplied the ancestor for its own ask and acquire returned True on a foreign clash without writing a claim. Fix: exclude the asker's own file from the ancestors dict (same exclusion line 833 already applies to 'held'). By-file not by-name: by-name would reintroduce the defect 58 fixed (a parent job's claim under a different name with a descendant asking under the same name is the same job). Defect 2 (harness.py:22996): unlink ran BEFORE acquire, so a refused acquire left the cards declared by nobody while the job ran on them — the de-47 hole the pending row exists to close, reopened at the moment it was needed. Fix: acquire first, unlink only on success, and only if the row's state is still 'pending' (acquire's O_EXCL rebind path reuses the file for the job pid, in which case unlinking would delete the real claim). On refusal the pending row STAYS, so the cards remain declared and go stale when the wrapper exits. Selftest: new world with foreign holder on card 6 + pending row + descendant ask, asserts refusal names the foreign holder. Two controls: foreign holder must have WRITTEN a file (otherwise vacuous), job pid must really be a descendant of the wrapper (otherwise ancestry test can't fire). Own claim dir to avoid selftest's own claims interfering. 144/144 pass. Mutants: control green, shipped defect RED, by-name RED.
artifact: card_claim.py --selftest: 144/144 pass, including selfx_* world at scripts/card_claim.py:2955

task: PR #23 (30753dd5) write token counts beside each cache so a pool can be sized beside a run
artifact: Read git show 30753dd5:scripts/write_mix_500m.py 472-530 and 30753dd5:train.py 2060-2086 from the branch, not the PR body. Then CONSTRUCTED and RAN two worlds against the merged tree (origin/main + 30753dd5, clean auto-merge, /tmp/pr23m): /tmp/w23.py rebuilds a real cache through _domain_seqs after a raise in the torch.save -> .counts window, and /tmp/w23b.py writes a well-formed .counts missing `seq`. The PR's own scripts/test_cache_counts.py is green on that tree.
verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED. Two defects, each reproduced by an executed world rather than argued from the source.
findings: (1) A STALE SIDECAR SURVIVES A REBUILD AND IS BELIEVED. train.py:2062's ordering argument -- 'a crash between the two leaves a cache with no .counts, which the reader treats as absent' -- holds only for a FIRST build. On a rebuild the previous sidecar is still on disk, so a raise between torch.save and the .counts write leaves a new tensor beside the old tensor's counts, and _cache_pool prefers the sidecar. Measured: 400 docs -> 800 docs with VOCAB_ID cleared so the file's own documented 'refusing to stamp' raise fires in the window; cache holds 7200 tokens, .counts says 3600, _cache_pool returns tokens 3600 pool_rows 380 source 'counts', silently, 2x off. seq/fone cannot catch it -- both unchanged; what changed is the corpus, which is what .srcfp covers and this sidecar does not. Fix offered: unlink the sidecar immediately BEFORE torch.save, so every failure in the window leaves the absent state the reader already handles. (2) A .counts MISSING `seq` ESCAPES AS AN UNCAUGHT KeyError. int(c['tokens']) is inside the try; int(c['seq']) at write_mix_500m.py:497 is outside it, and KeyError is in that except tuple precisely because this is the damaged-file class. Measured: KeyError 'seq' propagates out of _cache_pool, and _measured_pools calls it per domain, so one truncated sidecar kills the whole mix write instead of costing one expensive read. The test's damaged case writes '{not json' (ValueError) -- a well-formed object with a missing key is a different arm.
outcome: changes requested, two constructed cases posted at PR #23 comment 5579265277; also noted that 0 of 27 pod caches carry a .counts today, so the benefit arrives on the next retokenize rather than at merge

Also read the CALL SITE rather than the function alone: _assert_mix_derived_against is called from build_mix, which AGENTS.md states is the only data path, so a mix cannot reach training without passing it.
verdict: APPROVED. The design decision that makes this correct rather than merely present is the TRIPLE: rows alone do not identify a prefix, since the same row count over a re-fingerprinted corpus or a different sample seed is a different set of rows, and `epochs` would then be arithmetic over a prefix that no longer exists. Two asymmetries are right and each is the opposite of the obvious choice: every domain the MIX names rather than dict equality (mix_30b_stage2 renames en_c4 -> en_c4_stage2, so its 5 domains against a checkpoint's 7 would refuse the one resume it was written for), and fingerprints compared only over domains BOTH sides record (a checkpoint predating a domain carries no fingerprint, and refusing there is refusing on absence of evidence). M4's death confirms the first is load-bearing rather than incidental.
findings: None blocking. The accept path prints what it compared, which is the half that usually goes missing: a mix that UNDER-accounts by naming fewer domains passes silently under the superset rule, and the printed counts are what makes that visible to a log reader. Worth noting for whoever reads those logs that the line is evidence of coverage, not of correctness -- 'every checkpoint domain is accounted for' means the mix named them, not that its epochs arithmetic is right.
